# zeta-lab

> A computational laboratory for the Riemann zeta function: verified numerics,
> runnable demonstrations, and a written course covering the Riemann Hypothesis
> from the harmonic series to the research frontier. It is an instrument for
> building intuition, **not** a proof attempt — nothing computed here is
> evidence for RH, and `docs/08` explains why no computation could be.

Everything is Python + mpmath/Arb, tested against independent oracles. The
organising idea: theta is the heat kernel, Poisson summation gives its modular
identity, the Mellin transform turns that into the functional equation whose
mirror axis is Re(s) = 1/2, the explicit formula rebuilds the primes from the
zeros, and running the same heat flow on Ξ produces the de Bruijn–Newman
constant, where RH ⟺ Λ = 0 and Λ ≥ 0 is a theorem.

## Start here

- [README.md](README.md): front door — the door switchboard, quickstart, repo map.
- [docs/doors/README.md](docs/doors/README.md): one short page per way in
  (learn / refute / certify / discover / adopt) plus one per department. One
  spine, several doors: start here rather than reading README top to bottom.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): operating context for coding agents — setup, house
  rules, naming traps, honest-scope policy. Read before changing anything.
- [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md): the decisions — strategic bet, deliberate
  non-goals, known gaps, next build. Read before planning work.
- [CONTEXT.md](CONTEXT.md): generated index of the full API, docs, scripts and
  test counts. Regenerate with `python scripts/make_context.py`.
- [references/mathlib-open-targets.md](references/mathlib-open-targets.md):
  generated from Mathlib's own `docs/1000.yaml` — the famous theorems it
  records as wanted and unbuilt. The upstream track for `lean/`; judgment
  lives in ROADMAP.md. Regenerate with `python scripts/mathlib_gaps.py`.

## The written course (docs/, in reading order)

- [docs/00-orientation.md](docs/00-orientation.md): what RH says, what is known, honest scope.
- [docs/01-sums-integrals-and-continuation.md](docs/01-sums-integrals-and-continuation.md): the harmonic series, Euler–Maclaurin, ζ(−1) = −1/12.
- [docs/02-theta-heat-and-modularity.md](docs/02-theta-heat-and-modularity.md): theta as the heat kernel; Poisson summation.
- [docs/03-functional-equation.md](docs/03-functional-equation.md): modularity in, ξ(s) = ξ(1−s) out.
- [docs/04-explicit-formula.md](docs/04-explicit-formula.md): zeros ↔ primes as an identity.
- [docs/05-de-bruijn-newman.md](docs/05-de-bruijn-newman.md): heat flow on Ξ; RH ⟺ Λ = 0.
- [docs/06-hilbert-polya-and-gue.md](docs/06-hilbert-polya-and-gue.md): the spectral dream and random-matrix statistics.
- [docs/07-equivalences-and-criteria.md](docs/07-equivalences-and-criteria.md): statements equivalent to RH.
- [docs/08-why-it-is-hard.md](docs/08-why-it-is-hard.md): what each known technique provably cannot do.
- [docs/08-detector-strength-findings.md](docs/08-detector-strength-findings.md): how much a detector can actually see — power, measured.
- [docs/09-new-ontologies.md](docs/09-new-ontologies.md): what "RH needs new mathematics" means.
- [docs/10-trace-formulas-and-connes.md](docs/10-trace-formulas-and-connes.md): explicit formula as a trace formula.
- [docs/11-f1-and-the-missing-geometry.md](docs/11-f1-and-the-missing-geometry.md): the field with one element; Deninger.
- [docs/12-how-hard-problems-die.md](docs/12-how-hard-problems-die.md): how famous problems actually get solved.
- [docs/13-moments.md](docs/13-moments.md): external zero/value tables, finite moments, leading constants, and gated scorecards.
- [docs/14-how-new-mathematics-gets-invented.md](docs/14-how-new-mathematics-gets-invented.md): eleven ways new mathematics has been invented, scored against the Frobenius gap.
- [docs/15-the-f1-discovery-engine.md](docs/15-the-f1-discovery-engine.md): the F1 discovery engine.
- [docs/16-poisson-cokernel-plan.md](docs/16-poisson-cokernel-plan.md): the cokernel plan, and the experiment that closed the matrix route.
- [docs/17-the-falsification-harness.md](docs/17-the-falsification-harness.md): **the methods retrospective** — five claims of zero structure arrived in one day and standing instruments dispatched all five. Start here for the refereeing.
- [docs/18-five-longshots.md](docs/18-five-longshots.md): five longshot probes, each run to its wall.
- [docs/19-research-dossiers.md](docs/19-research-dossiers.md): the dossier probe — representing research state; §6 is why it is not a department.

## The referee (`harness/`)

- [harness/README.md](harness/README.md): the falsification protocol with the
  subject factored out. Four instrument roles — rivals (share the structure,
  lack the property), decoys (ablation), surrogates (null control), lesions
  (detector power) — bundled into a `Battery`; a `Department` is a battery plus
  a door plus reference claims with known verdicts.
- The admission rule: **no department without a battery.** A battery with no
  rival, with neither decoy nor surrogate, or with no lesion is refused,
  because it could never fail. Work nothing here can falsify is a probe, not a
  department.
- `harness/protocol.py` is domain-agnostic under the same three seam tests as
  `ontology/schema.py`; subject matter lives only in `harness/departments/`.
  `tests/test_department_conformance.py` is parametrized over the registered
  departments, so adding one adds its audit.
- The integrity layer ([docs/20](docs/20-verification-integrity.md)):
  batteries are themselves audited (`harness/integrity.py`, sixteen checks,
  five grades, no scalar), sham batteries are killed by name
  (`harness/shams.py`, `SHAM_MODES`), every claim outcome travels with its
  battery's integrity grade, and the audit's own blind spots are pinned in
  tests. Department #5 (`referee`) is the verification machinery as its own
  subject. `python -m harness.demo` runs everything, live.
- Entry point for a claim of your own: [docs/doors/refute.md](docs/doors/refute.md).

## Probes — not departments (`dossier/`, `hunts/`)

- The admission rule is **no department without a battery**. Work whose claims
  nothing in this tree can falsify is a *probe*, and probes are kept where
  nobody will mistake one for a result. Two live ones:
- [dossier/README.md](dossier/README.md) + [docs/19-research-dossiers.md](docs/19-research-dossiers.md):
  an experiment in representing research state — intent, definitions, rejected
  alternatives, semantic obligations, evidence — so an agent can resume rigorous
  work. Keeps four *independent* support axes (numeric / certified / literature
  / formal) and refuses to aggregate them; `Support.__bool__` raises. One worked
  example (Hardy Z), run with `scripts/50_dossier.py`.
- [hunts/README.md](hunts/README.md): scoped exploratory attacks, with
  permission to be wrong in public. Nothing in `hunts/` is a result.
- Neither can become a department by growing: their rivals are the *zeta*
  department's rivals, and a department whose battery is another department's
  battery is not a department.

## The conjecture factory (`ontology/`)

- [ontology/README.md](ontology/README.md): design document for the discovery
  funnel — five candidate kinds, six verdict states, the deduplication contract,
  what the schema cannot express, and the historical validation. A pipeline that
  logs itself so the conversion rate per generator can be measured: on a fresh
  ledger, 26 candidates → 20 already known, 1 trivial, 5 inconclusive, 0
  survivors. Run it with `scripts/13_discovery_run.py`.
- The seam: `schema/registry/ledger/funnel/metrics/historical_cases` are
  domain-agnostic and import nothing from `zeta`; `ontology/domains/` is the
  only place the subject is named. Enforced by tests.
- Honest scope: a survivor is a **lead**, never a result and never evidence for
  RH; "not recognised offline" is the absence of a lookup, never novelty; the
  ledger in `conjectures/` is gitignored and must never be published.

## The certified arm (`lean/`)

- Lean 4 + Mathlib package `ZetaLean`: theorems kernel-checked, never
  measured; zero `sorry`s required to count. Rung 1 (ground-truth values and
  the zero-free half-plane) is done; the ladder toward the Davenport–Heilbronn
  theorem is in `ROADMAP.md` and `HANDOFF.md`. Build: `cd lean && lake build`.

## Optional

- [references/papers.md](references/papers.md): annotated reading list.
- `scripts/`: numbered runnable demonstrations; `06_tour.py` runs the whole
  story in about ninety seconds.
- `figures/`: generated plots; rebuild with `scripts/make_figures.py --quick`.
